notes: SOURCE BLOCKED (AWS WAF challenge on digicoll /record/*, full diagnosis in the rancho-santa-rosa note). METHODOLOGICAL FINDING - THIS RECORD BREAKS THE UNFLAGGED-STRATUM PRIOR. Its hoffman_1862 block has governor: null and grantee: null. So hoffman_flags: [] here does NOT mean 'the 1862 printed table agreed with the register on governor and grantee' - it means Hoffman printed NOTHING to compare against. Any record whose Hoffman governor/grantee are null is unflagged by absence of data, not by agreement, and carries none of the reassurance the unflagged stratum is supposed to carry. The parent should re-partition the stratum on non-null Hoffman fields before quoting a 3% error rate; records like this one belong with the flagged priority set, not the clean set. SUBSTANTIVE FINDING: this is a TWO-GRANT case - Figueroa 1834 to Jose Tiburcio Castro (1 league) AND Pico 1845 to Jose Castro and Francisca Castro (2 leagues), with the 10,241.19-acre patent resting on both. The register records only the first, which is defensible as the originating grant but materially incomplete; the same shape appears in rancho-sausal-redondo below. RE-RUNNER: file is 51,952,712 bytes (smallest of the six); MARC 500$a 'Spanish text on pages 12-13, 16-17', so --pages 1-22 covers both expedientes. Bowman's patent line matches the register exactly: patent to Jacob P. Leese, Sept. 2 1859, 10,241.19 acres, GLO 264, recorded in Salinas. Associated Case Numbers per MARC: 'Toma 283, Filed Expediente 121, Docket 557, 190 SD, GLO 264' - Docket 557 = Hoffman commission_no 557, agrees. Hoffman also uniquely marks this one patented_1862: true, consistent with the 1859 patent date.
